To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) over-parameterized neural networks can be trained using gradient descent on linearly separable data and generalize to unseen data; (ii) the generalization behavior of such networks can be understood in terms of a simple linear model; and (iii) the generalization performance of this linear model is determined by the ratio between the number of training samples and the dimension of the data.

1) the generalization of deep learning is not understood; 2) the generalization behavior of deep learning is different from that of classical statistical learning methods; 3) the generalization performance of deep networks can be improved by adding noise or by using a larger network.
we propose a new training algorithm, SGD with momentum (SGDm), which provably generalizes to linearly separable datasets, and which can be implemented efficiently in parallel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to learn a good model for the task of predicting a real-valued target function.
the following questions: 1) How can we design a neural network architecture that can provably learn the target function in the over-parameterized regime?
the question of why neural networks generalize well.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current evidence does not support the hypothesis that overparameterization is the main reason for the success of deep networks.
over-parameterization is necessary for good generalization.
the over-parameterized deep neural networks can generalize well on linearly separable data, but not on non-linearly separable data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new framework for understanding generalization of over-parameterized neural networks.
we show that the generalization error in over-parametrized neural network is bounded by the Rademacher complexity of the network, and that this bound is tight in the worst-case.
over-parameterized neural networks are not just good at fitting the training data, they are also good at generalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
over-parameterized models can generalize well even when trained on a small number of samples.
we can train overparameterized networks with SGD to provably learn linear models.
we can learn over-parameterized neural network models that provably generalize on linearly separable data, even when trained with stochastic gradient descent.
